{"summary": "I added `word_count(text)` to `textutils.py`. It returns a plain dict that maps each lower-cased word to how many times it appears.

A word is any run of letters, digits and apostrophes, so `it's` and `o'clock` stay whole. Everything else separates words, including hyphens and underscores, so `late-ish` counts as `late` and `ish`. Letters from other alphabets count as letters, not just A–Z.

I also added three tests to `test_textutils.py`: mixed punctuation and case, empty or punctuation-only input, and underscores splitting words. `python -m unittest` passes all 4 tests.

One edge case: apostrophes at the start or end of a word are kept, so `'quoted'` counts as `'quoted'`, quotes included.", "outputs": ["textutils.py"], "suggestions": ["Strip leading/trailing apostrophes from words in word_count", "Add a most_common(text, n) helper"]}
